HDSN-5.rationale: AIM Act HFC consumption allowances are zero-sum and publicly allocated by EPA each year; the canonical adjudicator for any 'we received X% of total HFC allowances' claim is the EPA's published annual allocation notice itself. No other source can adjudicate this.
HDSN-5.note: score UNVERIFIABLE; connector not yet built

creative_extensions.signal_direction: an open recompete with new bidders signals contract-renewal risk; a direct award to Hudson would extend the federal revenue base

creative_extensions.source_label: AHRI Certified Directory (Air Conditioning, Heating and Refrigeration Institute)

creative_extensions.claim_text: Hudson received EPA AIM Act HFC allocation allowances for calendar years 2023 and 2024 equal to approximately 1% of total HFC consumption allowances, positioning it within the EPA's HFC phasedown fram
creative_extensions.source_label: EPA SNAP (Significant New Alternatives Policy) program acceptable-substitute determinations
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: https://www.epa.gov/snap — search by application + substitute refrigerant
creative_extensions.rationale: SNAP is the canonical EPA list of acceptable HFC alternatives by use sector. Hudson's reclaimed-HFC business model depends on which substitutes EPA has approved for which end-uses, so SNAP listings drive the addressable market.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: list of acceptable substitutes by application (retail food refrigeration, motor vehicle AC, residential AC, etc.) with HFC-blend identity
creative_extensions.signal_direction: this is a market-sizing observable rather than a direct claim test — supplements the AIM Act allocation claim

creative_extensions.claim_text: On June 6, 2024, Hudson's subsidiary Hudson Technologies Company acquired substantially all the business assets of USA United Suppliers of America, Inc. (d/b/a USA Refrigerants) and B&B Jobber Service
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: EDGAR — Hudson Technologies 8-K filings with Items 1.01 (material definitive agreement) and 2.01 (completion of acquisition) circa June 2024
creative_extensions.rationale: A $20.7M asset acquisition crosses Hudson's materiality threshold and triggers Item 2.01 reporting; a missing 8-K would be a disclosure-quality red flag.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: 8-K filing dated on/around 2024-06-06 with Item 2.01 reporting the USA Refrigerants close
creative_extensions.signal_direction: presence corroborates; absence would be a SEVERE disclosure-quality concern

creative_extensions.claim_text: On June 6, 2024, Hudson's subsidiary Hudson Technologies Company acquired substantially all the business assets of USA United Suppliers of America, Inc. (d/b/a USA Refrigerants) and B&B Jobber Service
creative_extensions.source_label: USA United Suppliers of America Inc + B&B Jobber Services Inc state-level corporate registries
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: state Secretary of State business entity searches in the states of formation
creative_extensions.rationale: Verify the acquired entities exist as real legal entities (not vehicle structures); confirm any post-acquisition status change (e.g., dissolved or merged into HTC).
creative_extensions.expected_observable: active or dissolved-via-merger corporate records for both targets
creative_extensions.signal_direction: presence + post-2024-06 status change corroborates a real consummated acquisition; absence would suggest paper-only assets

creative_extensions.claim_text: On June 6, 2024, Hudson's subsidiary Hudson Technologies Company acquired substantially all the business assets of USA United Suppliers of America, Inc. (d/b/a USA Refrigerants) and B&B Jobber Service
creative_extensions.source_label: claim_evolution to track post-close goodwill / impairment trajectory
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: claim_evolution.query_claim_evolution with cik=0000925528, search_term='USA Refrigerants', base_filing_date='2024-06-06'
creative_extensions.rationale: Goodwill from acquisitions is a leading-indicator distress class — if Hudson takes a goodwill impairment on USA Refrigerants in 2025-2026 10-Qs, that retroactively challenges the value of the acquisition and would show up as silent-or-restating disclosure evolution.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: ongoing mentions in 10-Qs (REAFFIRMED) vs going silent (SILENT_POST_CLAIM) vs explicit impairment language
creative_extensions.signal_direction: REAFFIRMED corroborates a productive acquisition; impairment or silence challenges it

creative_extensions.claim_text: Hudson has a $75M asset-based revolving credit facility with Wells Fargo Bank expiring March 2027, with FY24 working capital of $147.7M, cash of $70.1M (up from $12.4M YoY), no debt outstanding, $91.8
creative_extensions.source_label: Wells Fargo asset-based lending public commitment data (8-K Item 1.01 exhibits)
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: EDGAR — pull credit agreement exhibits from 8-Ks dated 2022-03-02 (Amended A&R), 2024-06-06 (First Amendment), 2024-10-23 (Second Amendment)
creative_extensions.rationale: ABL covenant structure (minimum-liquidity, springing FCCR, repurchase carve-outs) is the canonical lender-side signal for borrower stress. The Second Amendment expanded buyback capacity — that is an UPGRADE not a distress signal.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: credit-agreement covenants showing maintained liquidity headroom and increasing buyback permissions
creative_extensions.signal_direction: covenant relaxation in favor of buyback corroborates non-distress; covenant tightening or waivers would signal distress

creative_extensions.claim_text: Hudson has a $75M asset-based revolving credit facility with Wells Fargo Bank expiring March 2027, with FY24 working capital of $147.7M, cash of $70.1M (up from $12.4M YoY), no debt outstanding, $91.8
creative_extensions.source_label: Form 4 insider buying/selling around AIRO-screen window
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: EDGAR Form 4 filings for HDSN insiders (CEO, CFO, directors) over 2024-2025
creative_extensions.rationale: Insider behavior is a cross-check on the management's optimism vs. distress; in a genuine going-concern setup we would expect heavy insider selling, while in this case officers/directors own ~8% per the 10-K.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: ratio of insider buys vs sells; aggregate shares disposed vs acquired
creative_extensions.signal_direction: net buying or holding corroborates non-distress; heavy unwinding would re-open the distress thesis
